ana-cs: FYI Juno is stuck onboarding. Their web embed spikes 429s on initial user session load. can someone look?
devon-sdk: can you paste the exact error payload / which SDK version?
ana-cs: (sorry) ana-cs: SDK v0.9.3, using browser embed script in iframe, logs show repeated: HTTP 429 - "rate_limited" and sometimes "prefetch failed". Happens when customers open app and 6 tabs hit at once.
mike-platform: are they using ephemeral keys or server-signed tokens? also region?
ana-cs: ana-cs: ephemeral tokens from their auth server, TTL 60s. region = us-west-2.
devon-sdk: that TTL sounds short for concurrent tabs + preflight. browser flow: each tab does a preflight + ephemeral fetch; if TTL < backoff jitter window they'll all try refresh. can you share init snippet?
ana-cs: ana-cs: here's the init snippet they use: ```<script src="https://cdn.redwood.ai/embed.js"></script> <script> Redwood.init({ key: window.__JUNO_TOKEN, env: 'prod', concurrency: 6 }) </script>```
alia-sre: quick note: the JS SDK default client-side rate limiter is permissive; if tokens are short we see many simultaneous handshake calls.
devon-sdk: recommend: 1) increase ephemeral token TTL to >=300s if possible; 2) add client-side soft-splay so tabs don't preflight together; 3) reduce concurrency param or enable connection reuse / keepalive.
mike-platform: also check their proxy: are they re-using keepalive or opening new TCP per request? new TCP per tab will hit our ingress limits. small curl to share from their environment would help: ```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/handshake```
nana-cs: I'll ask them to run that. they said they use a proxy edge that terminates TLS and opens new upstream connections per request (no keepalive).
alia-sre: that explains it — without keepalive upstream you get connection churn which shows up as many short-lived sessions, triggering our rate checks. ask them to enable HTTP keep-alive / connection pooling in proxy.
devon-sdk: meantime we can push a gated client patch: SDK can detect multiple tab contexts and do a single shared preflight via localStorage mutex + randomized backoff. I can ship a patch to v0.9.4 tomorrow.
mike-platform: short-term mitigation: tell Juno to set concurrency to 1 on init, and add exponential jitter on client retries. also whitelist their account for a higher handshake window while they ramp.
nana-cs: ana-cs: raising account to handshake grace = true would help — can ops do that?
mike-platform: mike-platform: I can add a temporary grace flag for acct: juno-inc (acct id 8675309) for 48h. ping me if you need longer.
alia-sre: in parallel, please collect a small timeline from Juno: number of tabs, average session startup QPS, proxy conn settings, and sample HTTP headers for the handshake call (User-Agent, Connection).
devon-sdk: example header we expect: 
```
POST /v1/handshake HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral>
User-Agent: RedwoodJS/0.9.3 browser
Connection: keep-alive
```
nana-cs: noted. I'll schedule a 30m troubleshooting session with them tomorrow 10am PT. inviting devon for SDK tweaks.
sre-bot: incident-note: temporary handshake-grace applied to acct 8675309 by mike-platform at 1815001400. ticket# CS-8122.
devon-sdk: thanks. action items: (1) ana to get proxy headers + curl output, (2) mike to keep grace flag, (3) devon to post v0.9.4 branch with localStorage mutex and jitter, (4) alia to monitor ingress error rate.
nana-cs: ana-cs: will confirm after call. thanks all :thumbsup:
